title: Linear conditional information for proper agnostic VC learning
formal: Conjecture 6 of the cited paper asks whether there is a universal constant c>0 such that, for every binary class H of VC dimension d≥1 and every n≥d, a randomized proper learner A:(X×{0,1})^n→H has CMI_D(A)≤cd for every distribution D and E_A[loss(A(z),z)]≤inf_{h∈H}loss(h,z)+c√(d/n) for every sample z. The intended arbitrary-domain measurable-space convention remains to be specified; this is not yet a completed benchmark statement.
context: The original record grouped three conjectures from Steinke and Zakynthinou (2020). The remaining target recorded here is their agnostic proper-learning Conjecture 6. Haghifam, Dziugaite, Moran and Roy (2020), Theorem 4.2, refute the stronger proper realizable-learning Conjectures 7 and 8. Those two conjectures must not be advertised as open variants of this card. The intended measurable model for the arbitrary-domain question still needs to be fixed before this record satisfies the statement manifesto.

definitions: H is a nonempty set of functions X→{0,1}; a finite subset B⊆X is shattered when all its binary labelings are restrictions of functions in H. Its VC dimension is the maximum shattered cardinality. Proper means that every output belongs to H. For z=((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n, loss(h,z)=(1/n)Σ_i 1[h(x_i)≠y_i]. To define CMI_D, draw a supersample Z̃=(Z̃_i,0,Z̃_i,1)_{i=1}^n with 2n independent draws from D, and independent fair bits S=(S₁,…,S_n); feed the selected sample (Z̃_i,S_i)_i to A with independent randomness. Put W=A((Z̃_i,S_i)_i). CMI_D(A)=I(W;S|Z̃)=H(S|Z̃)−H(S|W,Z̃), with base-two conditional Shannon entropy of the finite random variable S. The learner may depend on H,n, but not on D. The source does not specify sigma algebras for arbitrary X,H, measurability of evaluation, or admissibility of learners and distributions; those choices affect the quantified statement. No domain restriction is silently added here.

sentences: Conditional mutual information measures what a learner’s output reveals about which examples were selected from an independent supersample.
The target is the proper agnostic-learning Conjecture 6 of Steinke and Zakynthinou: information O(d) and expected empirical excess loss O(√(d/n)).
Here d is the VC dimension, n is sample size, and the learner must work for every data distribution.
The paper’s separate proper realizable Conjectures 7 and 8 were refuted by Haghifam, Dziugaite, Moran and Roy in 2020.
Measurability conventions for the arbitrary-domain question remain to be specified, so this formulation is still marked unfinished.
